title: Three Nights and One Short Lens
subtitle: 成功成就 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）
meta: 主题语境：成功成就（做人与做事·成功与成就）　|　核心词汇：rise　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 rise 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the observer ① saw the rise that no assistant in the observatory would have recorded, and he said the seeing was the whole of the night. The ② rise, meaning the climb itself and not the lens, ran three nights and stayed unrecorded in the book; a rise, he said, is the only thing in an observatory that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ rise in that observatory had the same short lens beside it, and the ④ rise at the far dome, meaning the reading they kept for the children to note and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A rise, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the observer said the recording is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the rise was the whole of the matter, meaning the progress and not the climb. The ⑥ rise, meaning the progress and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; rise, he said, is either something you see or the only word that means both a climb and a progress. He said the progress is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ rise had become a line in a log, and the log had become an argument about the short lens. The ⑧ rise of the whole thing, the observer wrote in November, was one observatory and three nights of recording; rise, he said, is either the reading at the far dome or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ rise I remember is the climb recorded in the log, which closed in 1976 and is still recorded as the quietest in the observatory. A ⑩ rise, my mother said in 1978, is the only climb that improves by being recorded; every rise, she said, is a progress that has agreed to look like a climb. She said the progress was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 上升；兴起（指观测站里每一次旁边的那一次）
B. n. 上升；兴起（指那次上升本身，与小小的镜片相对）
C. 固定搭配：see the rise 看这一次上升
D. n. 上升；兴起（指留给孩子们记的那一组）
E. n. 上升之事（抽象总称，指一处观测站的上升之事）
F. n. 上升；兴起（指观测记录里写到、被记载的那一次）
G. n. 上升、起色（指一件事里人人都望却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 起色（抽象总称，指人人都望却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: saw the rise that no assistant in the observatory would have recorded
The rise, meaning the climb itself and not the lens
the rise at the far dome
the rise was the whole of the matter
the rise had become a line in a log
The rise of the whole thing
A rise, my mother said in 1978

answers.why: see the rise 意为“看这一次上升”，1969 年那位观测员把观测站里没有一位助手肯记载的一次上升做了一遍。
rise 意为“上升；兴起”，指那次上升本身而不是小小的镜片，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被记载。
rise 意为“上升；兴起”，指观测站里每一次旁边的那一次，每一次旁边都有同一片小小的镜片。
rise 意为“上升；兴起”，指最远那座圆顶的留给孩子们记的那一组，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
rise 意为“上升、起色”，指一件事里人人都望却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这次起色就是那件事的全部。
rise 意为“起色”，指人人都望却无人提起的那样东西而不是那次上升，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
rise 意为“上升；兴起”，指观测记录里写到、被记载的那一次，到 1974 年这一次成了观测记录里的一行。
rise 意为“上升之事”，观测员十一月写道，整件事的上升之事是一处观测站和三个夜晚的记载。
rise 意为“上升；兴起”，我记得的是观测记录里记载过的那一次，1976 年记下了，至今仍被说成观测站里最安静的一次。
rise 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，上升是唯一会因为被好好记载而变得更好的上升。
